decisions.trigger: 3m closed through its moving average AND through POC - two levels, so it clears the R1 minimum

decisions.value: THE HEADROOM RULE. Two levels broken is necessary but not sufficient - the next level beyond entry must not be immediately in the way. This is a genuinely new constraint.

declared_rules.rule: HEADROOM. Two levels broken is the minimum, not the criterion. The next level beyond the entry must not be immediately in the way.
declared_rules.quote: I don't really like taking trades where it has to break through something in order for my trade to work. I like a couple things to be broken through with some headroom.

declared_rules.rule: POC should be ALIGNED with the trade, not an obstacle it has to break.
declared_rules.quote: I'd rather POC be aligned with my trades rather than rely on my trade to break through it.

declared_rules.rule: In chop, require higher-timeframe alignment before taking anything.
declared_rules.quote: I'm not going to take anything until I see some higher time frame alignment that's going to show us going in one direction. There's no reason to trade like that for no reason.

declared_rules.rule: LIMIT LIFETIME - answers the standing open question. A limit rests about 10 minutes maximum, and is CANCELLED if price reaches a structural level before filling it.
declared_rules.quote: A limit will rest for maybe 10 minutes max. If it runs to a structural level and then fills me, I'm not very confident in that anymore... I would want it to get filled within a couple minutes. The limits get filled pretty quickly. If it hits some structural levels and then fills me, I'm more likely to lose.
declared_rules.worked_example: On N2 he limited the retest of the value area low. 'If we were to come to the VWAP middle band before filling my limit order, I would close that limit order.'
declared_rules.implication: A fill is only valid if it arrives QUICKLY and WITHOUT price first visiting the next structure. A late fill is a different, worse trade.

declared_rules.rule: WINDOW SEMANTICS. The window governs ENTRIES only. Open trades are held to target.
declared_rules.quote: You don't flatten trades when the window closes. My window would be realistically around 10:45. That doesn't mean I flatten trades. I just can't enter any trades after that. I can hold them until my targets get hit.

declared_rules.rule: Trail aggressively in chop: to beyond the wick of a candle that rejects your level against you.
declared_rules.evidence: L1 cut a 29pt loss to 13.25pt. Verified that the untrailed stop would also have been hit, so the trail cost nothing and saved 16pt.

resolved_open_questions.question: How long does a limit rest before he pulls it, and does he ever chase?
resolved_open_questions.answer: ~10 minutes maximum, and pulled early if price reaches a structural level before filling. He never chases - a late fill is treated as a lower-quality trade, not the same trade.

resolved_open_questions.question: How far does the NY_AM window really run?
resolved_open_questions.answer: Entries to ~10:45. Holding past it is fine and expected. Note: January's 10:51 entry is outside even this - flagged, not resolved.
